active_paradigms.idea: Replace the size-limited Steiner DP with an exact directed-Steiner MILP using scipy.optimize.milp
active_paradigms.description: The current program constructs a directed shared multicast tree: for at most 13 unique receivers it uses the classical subset dynamic program with merge states and reverse Dijkstra, then falls back to a greedy shortest attachment tree. This is strong because each selected edge is shared by all downstream destinations, but the 13-terminal cutoff means larger cases can be substantially suboptimal, and neither branch models link throughput or partition-level congestion. Formulate a directed Steiner arborescence as a mixed-integer linear program with binary edge-installation variables y_e and one unit of commodity flow f_(terminal,e) for every destination terminal. Require every terminal commodity to send one unit from src to that terminal, constrain f_(t,e) <= y_e, and minimize sum(cost_e * y_e), optionally adding a very small tie-breaker based on inverse throughput or hop count. This directly solves the same shared-edge cost model that the current DP optimizes, but without exponential subset enumeration and without a heuristic cutoff. After solving, retain edges with y_e near one, extract a src-to-dst path in the selected subgraph, and assign that valid path to each partition. If evaluation actually charges congestion or transfer duration, extend the model with partition/commodity flow variables and capacity constraints rather than assuming the same route can carry every partition simultaneously.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary shared data-transfer cost, especially instances with more than 13 receivers where the present greedy fallback is not globally optimal; secondarily use throughput as a tie-breaker or explicit feasibility constraint.
active_paradigms.cautions: The supplied wrapper exposes no evaluator internals beyond calling evaluator.py, so its exact aggregation of partition cost and throughput cannot be proven from the shown code. Only include finite-cost edges, remove incoming edges to src, and add a practical time limit because multi-commodity MILPs grow as terminals times edges. Ensure every destination has a graph path before adding equality-demand constraints; handle unreachable destinations consistently with evaluator expectations. Do not mistake a fractional LP solution for a topology: y_e must be integral and selected paths must be reconstructed from the integer solution.

active_paradigms.idea: Use NetworkX network_simplex on a partition-expanded capacitated flow graph to route partitions over different networks
active_paradigms.description: The existing algorithm gives every partition of every destination exactly the same tree path, so it receives sharing but completely ignores the stated goal of parallel paths and the throughput fields in G. Build a partition-expanded directed graph in which each data partition is represented as one demand unit, edge capacities are derived from throughput, and per-edge cost is the evaluator-relevant transferred-byte cost. Add node/edge copies or capacity gadgets so a physical link has one aggregate capacity across all partition commodities, while each destination-partition has a required delivery demand. Invoke networkx.network_simplex once to obtain a minimum-cost feasible integral flow, then decompose each delivered unit of flow into src-to-destination paths for BroadCastTopology. This is fundamentally different from choosing a single multicast tree: it deliberately splits partitions across parallel cheap links and prevents all partitions from oversubscribing the same bottleneck. It should be particularly valuable if the evaluator computes transfer time from edge flow divided by throughput, or rejects/penalizes flows exceeding edge throughput. A sharing discount can be approximately represented by adding a low-cost first-use capacity tier and higher-cost subsequent capacity tiers for each physical edge, provided that matches the actual evaluator's billing semantics.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Partition-level load balance, edge-capacity feasibility, and elapsed transfer time while minimizing total routed transfer cost.
active_paradigms.cautions: network_simplex is single-commodity, so a plain construction can accidentally permit flow intended for one destination to satisfy another; destination-specific sink layers or a super-sink construction must preserve destination demands before path decomposition. NetworkX demands use a sign convention: source supply is negative and sink demand is positive. Integer capacities must be scaled carefully from floating throughput, and zero/negative-cost cycles should be avoided. This model is preferable only when evaluator bills each partition transfer or models congestion; if it bills a physical multicast edge once regardless of downstream copies, the MILP/Steiner formulation is more faithful.

active_paradigms.idea: Generate throughput-diverse candidate routes with NetworkX shortest_simple_paths and assign partitions to distinct path families
active_paradigms.description: The current exact DP has an excellent sharing objective but is blind to alternative near-cost routes: it normally emits one path to each receiver and clones it to all partitions. For every destination, use networkx.shortest_simple_paths on a scalarized edge weight that preserves monetary cost as the dominant term while using a tiny inverse-throughput or congestion tie-breaker. Consume only a small bounded prefix of simple paths, discard candidates containing missing-cost edges, and classify candidates by their first expensive inter-cloud edge or by physical-edge overlap. Assign partitions round-robin or by current accumulated normalized load across the least-overlapping low-cost candidates, while retaining the common Steiner prefix whenever its edge is genuinely cheaper than duplicate source egress. This supplies actual parallelism without changing BroadCastTopology's expected per-destination/per-partition path representation. It is also a useful robust alternative if the evaluator measures a makespan-like completion time, since routing all partitions identically can make one low-throughput edge dominate despite its low dollar cost. Use the current Steiner-tree route as an always-available baseline candidate, and only select a divergent candidate when its evaluator-aligned cost/time estimate is better.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Avoid redundant use of a bottleneck by distributing partitions over low-cost, edge-disjoint or low-overlap routes; improve throughput utilization with minimal increase in monetary cost.
active_paradigms.cautions: shortest_simple_paths is a generator whose worst-case runtime can be large, so stop after a fixed small number of candidates per destination and avoid requesting paths for unreachable nodes. It does not itself perform the final assignment; the crucial policy is to track aggregate load per physical edge and reject candidates that would exceed throughput. A naive cost perturbation can change genuinely optimal cost paths, so keep the throughput term lexicographically tiny or first restrict candidates to a tight cost band. If evaluator counts shared edges only once, excessive path diversity can increase cost and should be used only where capacity pressure justifies it.
